  reactions, content, attached community polls, and settings. Every term says both
  of its audiences: the people registered on the landing page of its event, and
  the people who entered its room. A room which is no term of an event says
  nothing about registrations at all. The registration block opens the exact
  filtered `/admin/contacts` list and its shared CSV, vCard, and Book exports;
  it never creates a second contact table or serializer in workshop administration.
- `/admin/community` manages the permanent community, including polls, project
  moderation, participants, memberships, payments, and room analytics.
- `/admin/shortener` manages public short links, QR/UTM output, destinations,
  notes, search/filter/sort state, and private click history. Links are served
  by `/[shortcode]`; `/shortener` redirects to the admin page.
- `/admin/login` authenticates the single `admin` account with `ADMIN_PASSWORD`
  and a signed session cookie. All `/admin/*` pages and APIs require
  `requireAdminSignedIn`. `/admin` is the post-login dashboard.
- Other public/legal routes include `/contact`, `/data-deletion`, `/privacy`,
  `/terms`, `/dekujeme`, `/branding`, and the routes under `/k`, `/old`, and
  `/test`.

#### Shared community and workshop behavior

- Rooms lead to each other in both directions, through one identity hand-off. The
  community lists the terms and opens the room of each; an invited workshop room
  places its community link beside its materials as a special material for every
  participant, regardless of paid membership. Where a special material sits is
  decided once, in `lib/workshops/workshopSpecialMaterials.ts`: a card says where
  among the ordinary materials it belongs, and the invitation opens the material
  list of a participant who does not pay while it closes the list of a paying
  member. A membership which is not loaded yet leaves it where a participant who
  does not pay reads it. Both carry the connected member's
  name and email on, and an incomplete identity carries nothing rather than half
  of it. Which rooms invite is answered by
  `lib/workshops/workshopKindCapabilities.ts`; the community and project
  discussions do not. The invitation names the community's sections by the names
  the community itself uses.
- Community polls attached to workshops are shared. A normalized email gives a
  member one vote across the community and all attached workshops. An
  administrator can enable an Other answer: a member-written response becomes
  one shared, anonymous option and receives that member's vote atomically, so
  every room can vote for it; later poll edits keep member-written answers.
  Workshops may display and accept votes, but the community owns administration.
  Where a room puts its polls is decided once, in
  `lib/workshops/workshopPollPlacement.ts`: the community, which decides in its
  own polls, opens with them, while a workshop, which is only their subject,
  keeps them below the materials it was held for.
- The participant room owns the membership badge and popup. Community and live
  workshop rooms use the same membership for the connecting email, and checkout
  returns to the room where it started. Membership is offered only by room kinds
  listed in `lib/workshops/workshopKindCapabilities.ts`; project discussions do
  not offer it.
- Members can open Stripe Customer Portal from the popup. In-app cancellation
  stops only the next renewal, preserves access through the paid period, appears
  in the badge, and can be reversed before that period ends.
- A full-price-for-the-whole-term discount is a voucher: atomically consume it,
  create membership immediately, ask for no card, and create no Stripe renewal.
  A limited-month discount still opens checkout because the regular price returns.
  Stripe webhooks update completed, cancelled, failed, and late payments. With no
  Stripe key, hide membership; with test keys, identify the test payment gate.
- Community projects use a URL-first metadata wizard. Ordinary submissions await
  moderation; trusted members and moderators are approved immediately. Pending
  projects remain visible to their author and moderators.
- A live workshop room has countdown, YouTube stage, reactions, watching count,
  moderated chat, timed materials, and attached poll aggregates. An open-ended
  term runs until its recorded end; its stage does not end automatically. Admins
  can select, replace, clear, or create the displayed comment through the same
  private realtime channel used by reactions.
- A term can be about a project. The connection is one value — GitHub repository,
  the default branch, and one or more branch patterns such as `main`, `client-*`,
  `feature/*`, or `*` for all branches, plus an optional deployment URL — so it is
  set, changed, and unset at once and neither branch selection nor deployment
  outlives its repository. Room kinds which offer it are named in
  `lib/workshops/workshopKindCapabilities.ts`. The room shows the repository as a
  special material beside its ordinary materials for every participant, with its
  links and newest commits, marking those which arrive while a participant watches;
  a newly found commit is broadcast to active rooms and appears on the stage for
  ten seconds. A selection resolving to multiple branches is shown as a commit
  graph. Commits come from the public commit feed or keyless API, pooled once per
  server and cached through the revalidation window; an unreadable feed still
  leaves the room naming its project.
- A workshop can carry one public presentation URL for a PDF, PowerPoint file, or
  GitHub Markdown page. The room renders it beside ordinary materials through the
  shared material card, primary action, and QR code, for every participant without
  making it timed or membership-gated content.
- Paid-only materials are decided on the server in one pass. Members receive
  unlocked material; others receive only the published titles as an offer. An
  untitled item is not named, items are not named before their unlock time, and a
  room without membership hides paid-only items without naming them.
- After a workshop ends, its recording is server-gated to members. Others receive
  the published teaser, or a generic offer when no teaser exists; a term without
  a recording offers nothing. An administrator can set the recording's start
  offset in seconds, which applies only to that paid replay and never to the
  countdown or live stream.
- Trusted participants remain invisible and their messages are auto-approved.
  Moderators see pending messages, can approve/reject/correct/pin them, and can
  trust or silence authors. Workshop and community moderators are appointed in
  `/admin/workshops`; project authors moderate their own discussions.
- The room records whether each open browser is actively or passively attended
  from pointer, typing, scroll, and touch activity. Admin analytics distinguish
  active computer users from merely open tabs with dashed audience lines.
- The community's compact gallery shows its five highest-upvoted approved projects
  and links to the full gallery. Community landing content is read from the live
  room: expose only anonymous totals, approved messages, and shared projects;
  show member first names only. If the room cannot be read, show less content,
  not an error. Landing-page reactions are estimates based on recent room data.

#### Administration and data rules

- Event kinds are defined once in `lib/events/eventTypes.ts`; adding one should
  not require database migration or page-specific duplication. Terms ask for kind,
  online/place format, price, and capacity. Each kind also names where its landing
  page records registrations, which is the `placeName` of the contacts it gathers.
  A kind which names no landing page is held by somebody else: its terms carry the
  address they are held at, are refused without one, and this application runs no
  room, gathers no registration, and returns no payer to them.
- Which term a registration belongs to is decided once, in
  `lib/workshops/workshopRegistrations.ts`. A term is recognised by its slug, by
  its Prague day, and by the moment it begins at, so registrations written before
  terms had slugs keep counting. Registration forms write the term through the
  same line prefixes that rule reads back. Contacts are still gathered, recorded
  and shown only by `/admin/contacts`; counting reads nothing but their notes.
  The registration actions in workshop administration carry that same term filter
  into the contacts list and its exports.
- Workshop polls are read-only in workshop administration. Creating a new event
  publishes it by default; duplicating an event keeps it published unless the
  source is unpublished. Duplicating a workshop preserves its connections to
  the already existing attached polls; it creates no polls, options, votes, or room history. Stage settings contain

## Context

### Context

This repository contains Promptbook landing pages for different businesses,
use cases, and audiences. Keep these rules current when behavior changes.

#### Public routes

- `/` redirects to `/cs` or `/en` using `Accept-Language`.
- `/cs` is the Czech homepage and source of truth for homepage structure and copy.
- `/en` is its English localization.
- `/pro-mesta`, `/pro-firmy`, `/for-agro`, `/for-industry`, `/ai-supervize`,
  `/hackathon-factory`, and `/pavol` are specialized landing pages. `/pavol`
  redirects to `/cs/pavol` or `/en/pavol`; the localized pages are Pavol Hejny's
  personal pages.
- `/ai-supervize-mini` is the Czech one-day AI Supervize page. Published terms,
  prices, capacities, places, FAQs, registration, and participant information
  come from `/admin/workshops`; with no published term it shows a notice.
  `/skoleni` redirects there.
- `/cs/online-workshop` lists free 60-minute online workshops about writing
  production code with AI agents. Each term has its own subject and description,
  but all use one registration form. `/cs/online-workshop/dekujeme` is the
  full-load conversion page; `/participant` is the live room. Its waiting room
  offers every published term as the same term cards the landing page registers
  with: running and upcoming ones first, then the ones which ended within the
  last day, and the older finished ones behind a disclosure.
  Picking one changes the room being connected to and the `workshop` parameter,
  without losing the name and e-mail already typed. Once a term has its recorded
  end, its participant wrap-up offers a locally generated PDF using only the
  attendee-visible description, key takeaways and shared materials; it creates
  no administrative setting or database record.
- `/ai-ta-krajta` reads episodes hourly from podcast RSS and YouTube feeds and
  merges their host rosters with `businesses/ai-ta-krajta/aiTaKrajtaEpisodes.json`. Its shared platform list exposes
  the publisher's direct RSS feed for custom podcast applications, and page metadata advertises it as
  `application/rss+xml`.
  Each episode lists every credited person by name, and every person any source
  credits has a card in `aiTaKrajtaPeople.ts`, which a test keeps in step, so a
  credited person never misses their portrait and the filter cannot lose them.
  It keeps exact episode counts but labels subscriptions and listening hours as
  estimates. The fixed mini-player, newest-episode header button, person/search/
  episode/play/archive/collaboration filters, and section hash are shareable as
  query/hash state; the snake game is local state. Person clicks filter episodes.
  Everyone in the roster shows a normalized, transparent PNG portrait. The source
  crop is recorded by `scripts/_cutAiTaKrajtaPeoplePortraits.mjs`, from the
  episode cover the show itself published them on or from the picture they publish
  of themselves when no cover carries them; the final alpha PNG is named by the
  roster and a test verifies its format and transparent pixels. Portrait frames
  supply subtle, stable neutral-gradient variations and a restrained hover cue,
  so photographed backgrounds never compete with the page. The one people list
  is drawn anew
  for every visit, weighted by how many episodes of the archive name each
  person, so somebody heard often comes up high far more often than someone in
  one díl without the list ever becoming a ranking. The draw is local state and
  is made in the browser; the page itself is built in the order the draw leans
  towards, from the most often named person to the least often named one, so the
  browser hydrates into the list it was sent.
  Collaboration submissions use `/admin/contacts`. Its tab icon is the page's
  own snake drawing in `/ai-ta-krajta/logo.svg` and `.png`; SVG corners are
  rounded and transparent, while the raster fills its square. That drawing is
  traced off the cover artwork of the show and recorded once in
  `businesses/ai-ta-krajta/aiTaKrajtaMarkArtwork.ts`, together with the
  measurements of the animal along its own length. The snake of the minigame
  starts in exactly that shape, in the frame the still logo occupied, and only
  then eases into the proportions, colours and speed of a game snake.
  A seven-cell Promptbook coder terminal floats in the bottom-right corner and
  clears the player and cookie controls. It types `$ ptbk`, then animates an
  ASCII octopus in response to pointer, focus, scrolling, and the snake terrarium.
  It stays still for reduced motion and pauses its clock in hidden tabs. The
  badge and the shared footer credit link to `https://coder.ptbk.io/`.
- `/ai-ta-krajta/media-kit` and `/ai-ta-krajta/branding` are the two pages beside
  the podcast. They are named once, in `AI_TA_KRAJTA_SUBPAGES`, which the footer
  lists and which they point at each other through, so no link can name a page
  differently than the page names itself. Both wear the same compact header,
  section heading and footer as each other. The brand kit hands out the logo the
  site already serves at `/ai-ta-krajta/logo.svg`, `.png` and the cover artwork,
  publishes no colour outside `AI_TA_KRAJTA_COLORS`, and says how the name is
  written; it asks for nothing and sends visitors to the media-kit form.
- `/cs/komunita` is the permanent Czech community room. It has chat, polls,
  projects, materials, and published terms, but no schedule, stage, or live
  updates. Terms show event kind, format/place, price, and status. Where a term
  stands in time is decided once, in `lib/workshops/workshopPhase.ts`, as one of
  four phases: upcoming, ongoing, freshly past while it ended within the last
  `FRESHLY_PAST_WORKSHOP_HOURS`, and past. Every list, badge, and calendar colour
  reads that one answer, and everything which opens after a workshop — the
  wrap-up, the feedback, the recording — treats freshly past as over. A term with a
  live room links there; a term of an event held elsewhere opens its organizer's
  address in a new tab; otherwise it links to its landing page. The calendar
  opens on the member's month, can filter by day, and uses the same terms and
  statuses as the cards. Empty days cannot be selected; an empty month is only
  selected when the member's month has no terms. The room offers Google Calendar
  and `webcal:` subscriptions.
- `/cs/komunita/projects` is the full project gallery, ordered by upvotes.
  `/cs/komunita/projects/<project_id>` shows scraped project details and a
  moderated discussion. Project-room sessions derive from the community session;
  the author moderates their own discussion.
- `/cs/komunita/clenstvi` offers free community access and the 199 Kč monthly
  membership. Webinars remain free; paid access adds recordings, archive,
  materials, extra content, priority questions, and Discord/community features.
  The page is prefilled from `fullname` and `email`, supports community discount
  codes, has no new annual plan or trial, and allows cancellation.
- `/cs/komunita/calendar.ics` publishes the same terms by stable slug, so moved
  or renamed terms update existing subscriptions. It contains only event terms
  and public destinations, never subscriber identity.
- `/admin/workshops` manages terms of every event kind, participants, comments,
  reactions, content, attached community polls, and settings. Every term says both
  of its audiences: the people registered on the landing page of its event, and
  the people who entered its room. A room which is no term of an event says
  nothing about registrations at all. The registration block opens the exact
  filtered `/admin/contacts` list and its shared CSV, vCard, and Book exports;
  it never creates a second contact table or serializer in workshop administration.
- `/admin/community` manages the permanent community, including polls, project
  moderation, participants, memberships, payments, and room analytics.
- `/admin/shortener` manages public short links, QR/UTM output, destinations,
  notes, search/filter/sort state, and private click history. Links are served
  by `/[shortcode]`; `/shortener` redirects to the admin page.
- `/admin/login` authenticates the single `admin` account with `ADMIN_PASSWORD`
  and a signed session cookie. All `/admin/*` pages and APIs require
  `requireAdminSignedIn`. `/admin` is the post-login dashboard.
- Other public/legal routes include `/contact`, `/data-deletion`, `/privacy`,
  `/terms`, `/dekujeme`, `/branding`, and the routes under `/k`, `/old`, and
  `/test`.

#### Shared community and workshop behavior

- Rooms lead to each other in both directions, through one identity hand-off. The
  community lists the terms and opens the room of each; an invited workshop room
  places its community link beside its materials as a special material for every
  participant, regardless of paid membership. Where a special material sits is
  decided once, in `lib/workshops/workshopSpecialMaterials.ts`: a card says where
  among the ordinary materials it belongs, and the invitation opens the material
  list of a participant who does not pay while it closes the list of a paying
  member. A membership which is not loaded yet leaves it where a participant who
  does not pay reads it. Both carry the connected member's
  name and email on, and an incomplete identity carries nothing rather than half
  of it. Which rooms invite is answered by
  `lib/workshops/workshopKindCapabilities.ts`; the community and project
  discussions do not. The invitation names the community's sections by the names
  the community itself uses.
- Community polls attached to workshops are shared. A normalized email gives a
  member one vote across the community and all attached workshops. An
  administrator can enable an Other answer: a member-written response becomes
  one shared, anonymous option and receives that member's vote atomically, so
  every room can vote for it; later poll edits keep member-written answers.
  Workshops may display and accept votes, but the community owns administration.
  Where a room puts its polls is decided once, in
  `lib/workshops/workshopPollPlacement.ts`: the community, which decides in its
  own polls, opens with them, while a workshop, which is only their subject,
  keeps them below the materials it was held for.
- The participant room owns the membership badge and popup. Community and live
  workshop rooms use the same membership for the connecting email, and checkout
  returns to the room where it started. Membership is offered only by room kinds
  listed in `lib/workshops/workshopKindCapabilities.ts`; project discussions do
  not offer it.
- Members can open Stripe Customer Portal from the popup. In-app cancellation
  stops only the next renewal, preserves access through the paid period, appears
  in the badge, and can be reversed before that period ends.
- A full-price-for-the-whole-term discount is a voucher: atomically consume it,
  create membership immediately, ask for no card, and create no Stripe renewal.
  A limited-month discount still opens checkout because the regular price returns.
  Stripe webhooks update completed, cancelled, failed, and late payments. With no
  Stripe key, hide membership; with test keys, identify the test payment gate.
- Community projects use a URL-first metadata wizard. Ordinary submissions await
  moderation; trusted members and moderators are approved immediately. Pending
  projects remain visible to their author and moderators.
- A live workshop room has countdown, YouTube stage, reactions, watching count,
  moderated chat, timed materials, and attached poll aggregates. An open-ended
  term runs until its recorded end; its stage does not end automatically. Admins
  can select, replace, clear, or create the displayed comment through the same
  private realtime channel used by reactions.
- A term can be about a project. The connection is one value — GitHub repository,
  the default branch, and one or more branch patterns such as `main`, `client-*`,
  `feature/*`, or `*` for all branches, plus an optional deployment URL — so it is
  set, changed, and unset at once and neither branch selection nor deployment
  outlives its repository. Room kinds which offer it are named in
  `lib/workshops/workshopKindCapabilities.ts`. The room shows the repository as a
  special material beside its ordinary materials for every participant, with its
  links and newest commits, marking those which arrive while a participant watches;
  a newly found commit is broadcast to active rooms and appears on the stage for
  ten seconds. A selection resolving to multiple branches is shown as a commit
  graph. Commits come from the public commit feed or keyless API, pooled once per
  server and cached through the revalidation window; an unreadable feed still
  leaves the room naming its project.
- A workshop can carry one public presentation URL for a PDF, PowerPoint file, or
  GitHub Markdown page. The room renders it beside ordinary materials through the
  shared material card, primary action, and QR code, for every participant without
  making it timed or membership-gated content.
- Paid-only materials are decided on the server in one pass. Members receive
  unlocked material; others receive only the published titles as an offer. An
  untitled item is not named, items are not named before their unlock time, and a
  room without membership hides paid-only items without naming them.
- After a workshop ends, its recording is server-gated to members. Others receive
  the published teaser, or a generic offer when no teaser exists; a term without
  a recording offers nothing. An administrator can set the recording's start
  offset in seconds, which applies only to that paid replay and never to the
  countdown or live stream.
- Trusted participants remain invisible and their messages are auto-approved.
  Moderators see pending messages, can approve/reject/correct/pin them, and can
  trust or silence authors. Workshop and community moderators are appointed in
  `/admin/workshops`; project authors moderate their own discussions.
- The room records whether each open browser is actively or passively attended
  from pointer, typing, scroll, and touch activity. Admin analytics distinguish
  active computer users from merely open tabs with dashed audience lines.
- The community's compact gallery shows its five highest-upvoted approved projects
  and links to the full gallery. Community landing content is read from the live
  room: expose only anonymous totals, approved messages, and shared projects;
  show member first names only. If the room cannot be read, show less content,
  not an error. Landing-page reactions are estimates based on recent room data.

#### Administration and data rules

- Event kinds are defined once in `lib/events/eventTypes.ts`; adding one should
  not require database migration or page-specific duplication. Terms ask for kind,
  online/place format, price, and capacity. Each kind also names where its landing
  page records registrations, which is the `placeName` of the contacts it gathers.
  A kind which names no landing page is held by somebody else: its terms carry the
  address they are held at, are refused without one, and this application runs no
  room, gathers no registration, and returns no payer to them.
- Which term a registration belongs to is decided once, in
  `lib/workshops/workshopRegistrations.ts`. A term is recognised by its slug, by
  its Prague day, and by the moment it begins at, so registrations written before
  terms had slugs keep counting. Registration forms write the term through the
  same line prefixes that rule reads back. Contacts are still gathered, recorded
  and shown only by `/admin/contacts`; counting reads nothing but their notes.
  The registration actions in workshop administration carry that same term filter
  into the contacts list and its exports.
- Workshop polls are read-only in workshop administration. Creating a new event

  source is unpublished. Duplicating a workshop preserves its connections to

  the live stream, paid-recording start offset, and recording teaser; presentation settings the public presentation
  address, and project settings the repository the term is about, written as an
  address or as `owner/name`, together with its branch patterns. Deleting a workshop is a soft deletion: its room
  data and attached
  community polls stay stored, but the term leaves normal public and administrative

  room, section, lines, reaction, zoom, and keyword metrics through query params.
- Community administration is the workshop dashboard restricted to the
  `community` room kind: no room picker, schedule, stage, reactions, or address.
  Its membership view filters Stripe lifecycle, prices, discounts, identifiers,
  dates, test/live mode, and links to the exact Stripe checkout/subscription.
  Community analytics cover all measured time and member details show seen times.
- Shortener search, provenance filters, sorting, and selected click history live
  in GET parameters. Editing changes only shortcode, destinations, note, and
  landing page; deletion also deletes recorded clicks.

- Put database changes in `migrations/*.sql`. Startup and

My jsme, když jsme to začli, tak nebyl jakoby agent, to bylo prostě jakoby dostaneš odpověď a tady to vygeneruje kód. Všichni to dodělali. Já jsem říkal: „No tak chci dělat jako agentic approach. Prostě tohlecto je ten správnej. A udělali jsme ten bed. Takže jakoby jsme už šli do tohodle jako agent harness, agentic approach, to call a věděl jsem jakoby za roh, co se bude dít. A jakoby teď aktuálně v tom světě, když je někdo dobrej a dělá něco, tak ty firmy prostě mají zájem jako kupovat. To je vidět jakoby tady je fakt jako když děláš něco, co není úplně blbost, tak oni chtěj ten tým jako hodně. tohlecto nebyla akvizice s týrkou nebyla akvizice, že jako většina akvizic prostě je kvůli týmu a není to jakoby kvůli tomu produktu, ale prostě kvůli tomu týmu, který jakoby oni vysajou a využijou pro svůj prospěch. No, >> prostě se staneš jejich assetem. Eh >> jo jo jo, ale jakoby určitě každýmu bych doporučoval jakoby, kdyby jakoby je dobrý do něčeho skočit, něco tvořit, protože ty začneš cejtit jako, co se děje v tom trhu, pochopíš ten trh mnohem do větší hloubky a někdy bejt jakoby jedinečnej je velká nevýhoda, protože najednou skončíš tím, že děláš něco, co nikdo nechce. >> OK. A já jenom jenom doplňující otázka od Lukáše Cahy, kterej u nás byl minulej týden. Eh jestli jste věděli v červnu 2025, když byl Vibe Coding Hackaton, že budete exitovat? >> Samozřejmě, že ne. Jakoby jako jako tak já já ten produkt nebo to, co děláme jakoby mě baví, chci v tom pokračovat, ale nevěděl jsem, že to dopadne takhle. >> A jsem rád, že to jako nějak takhle dopadlo, ale i kdybysme neexitovali, tak prostě bysme v tom pokračovali a bylo by to taky sluníčkový. >> Tak předávám slovo dál. Ty jsi [odkašlání] už tou dobou teda byl v San Francisku, když se řešil ten exit nebo jak to jaká byla vlastně jako timeline steer codu? >> Jo, to ne, to jsme byli to jsme byli tady v Česku, my jsme fundraisovali, to bylo léto minulýho roku, kde jsme jakoby dělali fundraising. Konec září říjen jsme to řešili intenzivně, protože jsme dostali jakoby napítku od pár firem, že a co kdybysme vás koupili místo fundraingu? A my jsme zablo, hm, tak nevím. No >> a pak jsme to začali jakoby explorovat víc do hloubky a ono je někdy dobrý, já vím, že ta moje journey a to, že dělám startupy bude pokračovat, že tohlecto není jako konec, tohlecto je začátek, [smích] ale bylo dobrý i pro mě jakoby selfishly si udělat tohlencten exit, protože kvůli třeba budoucnosti a dalším investorům, ono to je vždycky jako užitečný mít jako aspoň něco, nějakej jako zářez, protože ono je rozdíl mezi prodejem a neprodejem a úspěchem a neúspěchem startupu tak thin line, že to není možný. Ale ty zkušenosti, který získáváš, jsou přenositelný extrémně. Takže ono to bylo takový trošku jako selfish rozhodnutí možná. A taky jsem viděl, že ten trh se hodně mění a že bysme museli pivotovat hrázně týrkout. To jsem jako viděl extrémně a vlastně někdo chtěl s týrkout tak, jak je, tak jsme mohli u toho pivotovat jinde než pod námi. >> Takže jsi velmi rád, že jsi prodal ten moment, kdy jsi prodal. Nemáš žádné eh pochybnosti o tom, že jste to mohli držet dýl a expandovat víc a tak, >> ne? To bude v tom dalším startupu. >> Dobře, [smích] budeme. >> To my moc děkujeme, že j tady byl. Myslím, že to bylo fakt inspirativní. Zároveň to bude asi jeden z nejdelších dílů, možná úplně nejdelší. Každopádně eh pro diváky dáme odkazy do popisku a určitě jako určitě se jako ptejte dál a jako říkejte, co byste jako co byste chtěli slyšet v dalších epizodách, případně koho byste chtěli slyšet v dalších epizodách. A my se loučíme s dílem 45 a těšíme se na dílu 46. Ahoj. >> Čau kluci. Díky. Bylo to super s vámi pokecat. Mějte se. Jdeme ke agentů. Ciao. Ciao. >> Ciao."

A room\n *       which lasts for days is measured more coarsely, so that the answer stays small however long it has been open.\n */\nfunction getWorkshopAdminTimelineBucketDurationSeconds(workshopRow: WorkshopRow): number {\n    const startsAtMilliseconds = Date.parse(workshopRow.starts_at);\n    const currentMilliseconds = Date.now();\n    const configuredEndsAtMilliseconds =\n        workshopRow.ends_at === null ? currentMilliseconds : Date.parse(workshopRow.ends_at);\n    const endsAtMilliseconds = Math.max(startsAtMilliseconds, configuredEndsAtMilliseconds);\n    const durationMilliseconds = endsAtMilliseconds - startsAtMilliseconds;\n\n    if (durationMilliseconds <= 2 * 60 * 60 * 1_000) {\n        return 60;\n    }\n\n    if (durationMilliseconds <= 8 * 60 * 60 * 1_000) {\n        return 300;\n    }\n\n    if (durationMilliseconds <= 3 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1_000) {\n        return 900;\n    }\n\n    if (durationMilliseconds <= 30 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1_000) {\n        return 3_600;\n    }\n\n    return 86_400;\n}\n\nfunction getWorkshopAdminTimelineEndsAt(workshopRow: WorkshopRow): string {\n    const startsAtMilliseconds = Date.parse(workshopRow.starts_at);\n    const endsAtMilliseconds = workshopRow.ends_at === null ? Every state reload and every heartbeat of every\n *       participant would otherwise count the whole audience for nobody to read.\n * Note: An unavailable count must never take the whole room down with it, so a failure is reported as nobody watching.\n */\nexport async function countWatchingWorkshopParticipants(\n    supabase: SupabaseClient,\n    workshopRow: WorkshopRow,\n): Promise<number> {\n    if (!isWorkshopPanelOffered(workshopRow.room_kind, workshopRow.disabled_panels, 'watching-count')) {\n        return 0;\n    }\n\n    const watchingSince = new Date(Date.now() - WORKSHOP_WATCHING_WINDOW_SECONDS * 1_000).toISOString();\n    const { count, error } = await supabase\n        .from(WORKSHOP_PARTICIPANT_TABLE_NAME)\n        .select('id', { count: 'exact', head: true })\n        .eq('workshop_id', workshopRow.id)\n        .gte('last_seen_at', watchingSince);\n\n    if (error) {\n        console.error('Failed to count the participants watching a workshop:', error.message);\n        return 0;\n    }\n\n    return (count ?? 0) + Math.max(0, workshopRow.artificial_watching_participant_count ?? 0);\n}\n\ntype LoadedWorkshopReactionCounts = {\n    readonly reactionCounts: readonly WorkshopReactionCount[];\n    readonly errorMessage: string | null;\n};\n\n/**\n * Loads the totals shown beside the reactions which a room currently offers\n *\n * Note: When the reactions panel is hidden, nobody can read these totals. errorMessage: null,\n    };\n}\n\n/**\n * Loads one page of participants together with the activity totals used for its sortable columns.\n *\n * Note: The database applies the filters and sort before supabase: SupabaseClient,\n    workshopId: string,\n    query: WorkshopAdminParticipantQuery,\n): Promise<{ readonly page: WorkshopAdminParticipantPage | null; readonly errorMessage: string | null }> {\n    const participantPageParameters = {\n        target_workshop_id: workshopId,\n        target_search_query: query.searchQuery,\n        target_is_trusted: query.isTrusted,\n        target_is_moderator: query.isModerator,\n        target_is_interaction_banned: query.isInteractionBanned,\n        target_registered_from: query.registeredFrom,\n        target_registered_to: return {\n            page: null,\n            errorMessage: reportSupabaseError(\n                `\\`${WORKSHOP_ADMIN_PARTICIPANT_PAGE_FUNCTION_NAME}\\``,\n                error,\n Shortened\n * material links are shareable, so they correctly belong to the material-wide\n * aggregate instead of this participant-attributed timeline.\n */\nexport async function .eq('participant_id', participantId)\n                .order('created_at', { ascending: true })\n                .order('id', { ascending: true })\n                .range(fromIndex, toIndex),\n        ),\n        loadAllSupabaseRows<WorkshopCommentUpvoteRow>((fromIndex, toIndex) =>\n            supabase\n                .from(WORKSHOP_UPVOTE_TABLE_NAME)\n                .select('id, comment_id, commentsResult.errorMessage ??\n        reactionsResult.errorMessage ??\n        upvotesResult.errorMessage ??\n        null;\n    if (firstErrorMessage !== null) {\n        return { timeline: null, errorMessage: firstErrorMessage };\n    }\n\n    if (participantResult.data === null) {\n        return { timeline: null, errorMessage: null };\n    }\n\n    const participant = participantResult.data as WorkshopAdminParticipantRow;\n    const commentRows = commentsResult.rows ?? []).map((comment) => [comment.id, comment] as const),\n    );\n    const events: WorkshopParticipantTimelineEvent[] = [\n        { kind: 'joined' as const, id: `joined-${participant.id}`, occurredAt: participant.connected_at },\n        { kind: 'last-seen' as const, id: `last-seen-${participant.id}`, occurredAt: participant.last_seen_at },\n        ...commentRows.map((comment): WorkshopParticipantTimelineEvent => ({\n            kind: 'comment',\n            id: comment.id,\n            occurredAt: comment.created_at,\n            body: comment.body,\n            status: comment.status,\n        })),\n        ...reactionRows.map((reaction): WorkshopParticipantTimelineEvent => ({\n            kind: 'reaction',\n            id: reaction.id,\n            occurredAt: reaction.created_at,\n            emoji: reaction.emoji,\n        })),\n        ...upvoteRows.map((upvote): WorkshopParticipantTimelineEvent => {\n            const comment = upvotedCommentById.get(upvote.comment_id);\n            return {\n                kind: 'upvote',\n                id: upvote.id,\n                occurredAt: upvote.created_at,\n                commentId: upvote.comment_id,\n                commentAuthorName: comment?.author_name ?? A very busy room is sampled from its newest messages, because those are the ones a\n *       graph of it is read for.\n */\nasync function loadWorkshopAdminCommentSamples(\n    supabase: SupabaseClient,\n    workshopRow: WorkshopRow,\n): Promise<{\n    readonly commentSamples: readonly WorkshopAdminCommentSample[] | null;\n    readonly isCommentSampleComplete: boolean;\n    readonly errorMessage: string | null;\n}> {\n    const { data, error } = await supabase\n        .from(WORKSHOP_COMMENT_TABLE_NAME)\n        .select('body, created_at')\n        .eq('workshop_id', workshopRow.id)\n        .order('created_at', { ascending: false })\n        .limit(MAXIMAL_WORKSHOP_ADMIN_COMMENT_SAMPLE_COUNT + 1);\n\n    if (error) {\n        return { commentSamples: null, isCommentSampleComplete: false, errorMessage: error.message };\n    }\n\n    const rows = (data ?? []) as WorkshopAdminCommentSampleRow[];\n    const isCommentSampleComplete = rows.length <= MAXIMAL_WORKSHOP_ADMIN_COMMENT_SAMPLE_COUNT;\n\n    return {\n        commentSamples: rows\n            .slice(0, MAXIMAL_WORKSHOP_ADMIN_COMMENT_SAMPLE_COUNT)\n            .map((row) => ({ occurredAt: row.created_at, body: row.body }))\n            .reverse(),\n        isCommentSampleComplete,\n        errorMessage: null,\n    };\n}\n\n/**\n * Loads compact workshop-wide timeline buckets and reaction totals for the overview and reactions sections.\n */\nexport async function loadWorkshopAdminAnalytics(\n    supabase: SupabaseClient,\n    workshopRow: WorkshopRow,\n): Promise<{ readonly analytics: WorkshopAdminAnalytics | null; readonly errorMessage: string | null }> {\n    const bucketDurationSeconds = getWorkshopAdminTimelineBucketDurationSeconds(workshopRow);\n    const timelineArguments = {\n        target_workshop_id: workshopRow.id,\n        target_bucket_seconds: bucketDurationSeconds,\n    };\n    const [timelineResult, reactionTimelineResult, reactionCountsResult, commentSampleResult] = await Promise.all([\n        supabase.rpc('get_workshop_admin_timeline', timelineArguments),\n        supabase.rpc('get_workshop_admin_reaction_timeline', timelineArguments),\n        supabase.rpc('get_workshop_reaction_counts', { target_workshop_id: workshopRow.id }),\n        loadWorkshopAdminCommentSamples(supabase, workshopRow),\n    ]);\n    const firstError =\n        timelineResult.error ??\n        reactionTimelineResult.error ??\n        reactionCountsResult.error ??\n        (commentSampleResult.errorMessage === null ? null : { message: commentSampleResult.errorMessage });\n    if (firstError) {\n        return { analytics: null, errorMessage: firstError.message };\n    }\n\n    const reactionCountsByBucket = groupWorkshopAdminReactionTimelineRows(\n        (reactionTimelineResult.data ?? [],\n            isCommentSampleComplete: commentSampleResult.isCommentSampleComplete,\n        },\n        errorMessage: null,\n    };\n}\n\n/**\n * Loads every participant which matches the [...firstPageResult.page.participants];\n    const totalPageCount = Math.ceil(firstPageResult.page.totalCount / exportQuery.pageSize);\n    for (let currentPage = 2; currentPage <= totalPageCount; return { participants, errorMessage: null };\n}\n\n/**\n * Loads all comments for a CSV export, without inheriting the short moderation list used by the interactive screen.\n */\nexport async function []) as WorkshopContentRow[]).map((contentBlock) =>\n            mapWorkshopContentRow(contentBlock, linkClickCountByContentBlockId.get(contentBlock.id) ?? 0),\n        ),\n        errorMessage: null,\n    };\n}\n\n/**\n * Lists the feedback from one workshop only for the administration.\n *\n * Feedback and participants stay separate source records, just as comments and reactions do. The small identity read\n * keeps this list attributable without ever exposing an e-mail address through the participant-facing state route.\n */\nexport async function loadWorkshopAdminFeedback(\n    supabase: SupabaseClient,\n    workshopId: string,\n): Promise<{ readonly feedbacks: readonly WorkshopAdminFeedback[] | null; readonly errorMessage: string | null }> {\n    const feedbackResult = await loadAllSupabaseRows<WorkshopFeedbackRow>(\n        (fromIndex, toIndex) =>\n            supabase\n                .from(WORKSHOP_FEEDBACK_TABLE_NAME)\n           .range(fromIndex, toIndex),\n        `the feedback of workshop ${workshopId}`,\n    );\n    if (feedbackResult.rows === null) {\n        return { feedbacks: null, errorMessage: .filter((feedback): feedback is WorkshopAdminFeedback => feedback !== null),\n        errorMessage: null,\n    };\n}\n\n/**\n * Loads the message pinned on top of a chat, whatever its age and Note: A pin which could not be loaded must never take the whole room down with it, so a failure is reported as\n *       nothing being pinned.\n */\nasync function return null;\n    }\n\n    const { data, error } = await supabase\n        .from(WORKSHOP_COMMENT_TABLE_NAME)\n        .select(WORKSHOP_COMMENT_COLUMNS)\n        .eq('id', workshopRow.pinned_comment_id)\n        .eq('workshop_id', workshopRow.id)\n        .maybeSingle();\n\n    if (error) {\n        console.error('Failed to load the pinned comment of a workshop:', error.message);\n        return null;\n    }\n\n    return data as WorkshopCommentRow | null;\n}\n\n/**\n * Adds the pinned message to the loaded ones, so the room keeps a pin on top however old it WorkshopCommentRow[],\n    pinnedCommentRow: WorkshopCommentRow | null,\n): readonly WorkshopCommentRow[] {\n    if (\n        pinnedCommentRow === null ||\n        pinnedCommentRow.status !== message on top of a chat or releases the top of that chat again\n *\n * Note: The workshop remembers a single pin, so pinning a message releases the previously pinned one in the same write.\n * Note: Releasing the top only clears this very message, so it never drops a pin which another tab set meanwhile.\n */\nexport async function updatePinnedWorkshopComment(\n    supabase: SupabaseClient,\n pinnedCommentQuery.eq('pinned_comment_id', commentId));\n    if (error) {\n        console.error('Failed to change the pinned comment of a workshop:', error.message);\n        return { errorMessage: 'Pinned comment could not be changed' };\n    }\n\n    return { errorMessage: null };\n}\n\n/**\n * Chooses the one comment the host is answering over the stage, or leaves the stage without a question.\n *\n * Note: The database checks that a selected comment belongs to this room. The stage keeps no copied text: the selected\n *       comment remains the one source of the question in both chat and live presentation.\n */\nexport async function updateWorkshopStageComment(\n    supabase: SupabaseClient,\n    workshopId: string,\n    stageCommentId: string | null,\n): Promise<{ readonly errorMessage: string | null }> {\n    const { error } = await supabase\n        .from(WORKSHOP_TABLE_NAME)\n        .update({ stage_comment_id: stageCommentId })\n        .eq('id', workshopId);\n    if (error) {\n        console.error('Failed to change the comment on a workshop stage:', error.message);\n        return { errorMessage: 'Stage comment could not be changed' };\n    }\n\n    return { errorMessage: null };\n}\n\nexport async function loadWorkshopPublicState(\n    supabase: SupabaseClient,\n    workshopRow: WorkshopRow,\n    participant: WorkshopParticipant,\n    commentSort: WorkshopCommentSort,\n): Promise<LoadedWorkshopPublicState> {\n    const contentVisibilityCutoff = new Date().toISOString();\n    const workshop = mapWorkshopRow(workshopRow);\n    const isWorkshopPast = workshopRow.room_kind === 'workshop' && getWorkshopPhase(workshop) === 'past';\n\n    // Note: The reactions which flew over the stage recently are replayed for somebody entering the room. A room\n    //       without that panel therefore does not load them, exactly as it does not count them.\n    const isReactionsPanelOffered = isWorkshopPanelOffered(\n        workshopRow.room_kind,\n        workshopRow.disabled_panels,\n        'reactions',\n    );\n    const roomCapabilities = getWorkshopKindCapabilities(workshopRow.room_kind);\n    const isStageOffered = roomCapabilities.isStageOffered;\n\n    // Note: The membership decides which materials a member sees, so the room asks about it before it assembles what\n    //       is visible. A room which does not offer the membership has nothing to unlock, and an answer which does\n    //       not arrive keeps the paid materials hidden rather than letting them escape.\n    let isPaidMember = false;\n    if (roomCapabilities.isMembershipOffered) {\n        const { membership, errorMessage: membershipErrorMessage } = await loadCommunityMembershipByEmail(\n            supabase,\n            participant.email,\n        );\n        if (membershipErrorMessage !== null) {\n            console.error('Failed to load the community membership of a workshop participant:', membershipErrorMessage);\n        }\n        isPaidMember = membership !== null && isPaidCommunityMembershipStatus(membership.status);\n    }\n\n    // Note: A moderator is shown every message which waits for a decision, because making that decision is exactly\n    //       what they are in the room for. Every state reload and every heartbeat of every\n *       participant would otherwise count the whole audience for nobody to read.\n * Note: An unavailable count must never take the whole room down with it, so a failure is reported as nobody watching.\n */\nexport async function countWatchingWorkshopParticipants(\n    supabase: SupabaseClient,\n    workshopRow: WorkshopRow,\n): Promise<number> {\n    if (!isWorkshopPanelOffered(workshopRow.room_kind, workshopRow.disabled_panels, 'watching-count')) {\n        return 0;\n    }\n\n    const watchingSince = new Date(Date.now() - WORKSHOP_WATCHING_WINDOW_SECONDS * 1_000).toISOString();\n    const { count, error } = await supabase\n        .from(WORKSHOP_PARTICIPANT_TABLE_NAME)\n        .select('id', { count: 'exact', head: true })\n        .eq('workshop_id', workshopRow.id)\n        .gte('last_seen_at', watchingSince);\n\n    if (error) {\n        console.error('Failed to count the participants watching a workshop:', error.message);\n        return 0;\n    }\n\n    return (count ?? 0) + Math.max(0, workshopRow.artificial_watching_participant_count ?? 0);\n}\n\ntype LoadedWorkshopReactionCounts = {\n    readonly reactionCounts: readonly WorkshopReactionCount[];\n    readonly errorMessage: string | null;\n};\n\n/**\n * Loads the totals shown beside the reactions which a room currently offers\n *\n * Note: When the reactions panel is hidden, nobody can read these totals. errorMessage: null,\n    };\n}\n\n/**\n * Loads one page of participants together with the activity totals used for its sortable columns.\n *\n * Note: The database applies the filters and sort before it limits the result, so a large workshop never needs to send\n * every participant to the browser just to display one page.\n */\nexport async function loadWorkshopAdminParticipantPage(\n    supabase: SupabaseClient,\n    workshopId: string,\n    query: WorkshopAdminParticipantQuery,\n): Promise<{ readonly page: WorkshopAdminParticipantPage | null; readonly errorMessage: string | null }> target_is_moderator: query.isModerator,\n        target_is_interaction_banned: query.isInteractionBanned,\n        target_registered_from: query.registeredFrom,\n        target_registered_to: .eq('participant_id', participantId)\n                .order('created_at', { ascending: true })\n                .order('id', { ascending: true })\n                .range(fromIndex, toIndex),\n        ),\n        loadAllSupabaseRows<WorkshopCommentUpvoteRow>((fromIndex, toIndex) =>\n            supabase\n                .from(WORKSHOP_UPVOTE_TABLE_NAME)\n                .select('id, comment_id, commentsResult.errorMessage ??\n        reactionsResult.errorMessage ??\n        upvotesResult.errorMessage ??\n        null;\n    if (firstErrorMessage !== null) {\n        return { timeline: null, []).map((comment) => [comment.id, comment] as const),\n    );\n    const events: WorkshopParticipantTimelineEvent[] = [\n        { kind: 'joined' as const, id: `joined-${participant.id}`, occurredAt: participant.connected_at },\n        { kind: 'last-seen' as const, id: `last-seen-${participant.id}`, occurredAt: participant.last_seen_at },\n        ...commentRows.map((comment): WorkshopParticipantTimelineEvent => ({\n            kind: 'comment',\n            id: comment.id,\n            occurredAt: comment.created_at,\n            body: comment.body,\n            status: comment.status,\n        })),\n        ...reactionRows.map((reaction): WorkshopParticipantTimelineEvent => ({\n            kind: 'reaction',\n            id: reaction.id,\n            occurredAt: reaction.created_at,\n            emoji: reaction.emoji,\n        })),\n        ...upvoteRows.map((upvote): WorkshopParticipantTimelineEvent => {\n            const comment = upvotedCommentById.get(upvote.comment_id);\n            return {\n                kind: 'upvote',\n                id: upvote.id,\n                occurredAt: upvote.created_at,\n                commentId: upvote.comment_id,\n                commentAuthorName: comment?.author_name ?? A very busy room is sampled from its newest messages, because those are the ones a\n *       graph of it is read for.\n */\nasync function loadWorkshopAdminCommentSamples(\n    supabase: SupabaseClient,\n    workshopRow: WorkshopRow,\n): Promise<{\n    readonly commentSamples: readonly WorkshopAdminCommentSample[] | null;\n    readonly isCommentSampleComplete: boolean;\n    readonly errorMessage: string | null;\n}> {\n    const { data, error } = await supabase\n        .from(WORKSHOP_COMMENT_TABLE_NAME)\n        .select('body, created_at')\n        .eq('workshop_id', workshopRow.id)\n        .order('created_at', { ascending: false })\n        .limit(MAXIMAL_WORKSHOP_ADMIN_COMMENT_SAMPLE_COUNT + 1);\n\n    if (error) {\n        return { commentSamples: null, isCommentSampleComplete: false, errorMessage: error.message };\n    }\n\n    const rows = (data ?? []) as WorkshopAdminCommentSampleRow[];\n    const isCommentSampleComplete = rows.length <= MAXIMAL_WORKSHOP_ADMIN_COMMENT_SAMPLE_COUNT;\n\n    return {\n        commentSamples: rows\n            .slice(0, MAXIMAL_WORKSHOP_ADMIN_COMMENT_SAMPLE_COUNT)\n            .map((row) => ({ occurredAt: row.created_at, body: row.body }))\n            .reverse(),\n        isCommentSampleComplete,\n        errorMessage: null,\n    };\n}\n\n/**\n * Loads compact workshop-wide timeline buckets and reaction totals for the overview and reactions sections.\n */\nexport async function loadWorkshopAdminAnalytics(\n    supabase: SupabaseClient,\n    workshopRow: WorkshopRow,\n): Promise<{ readonly analytics: WorkshopAdminAnalytics | null; readonly errorMessage: string | null }> {\n    const bucketDurationSeconds = getWorkshopAdminTimelineBucketDurationSeconds(workshopRow);\n    const timelineArguments = {\n        target_workshop_id: workshopRow.id,\n        target_bucket_seconds: bucketDurationSeconds,\n    };\n    const [timelineResult, reactionTimelineResult, reactionCountsResult, commentSampleResult] = await Promise.all([\n        supabase.rpc('get_workshop_admin_timeline', timelineArguments),\n        supabase.rpc('get_workshop_admin_reaction_timeline', timelineArguments),\n        supabase.rpc('get_workshop_reaction_counts', { target_workshop_id: workshopRow.id }),\n        loadWorkshopAdminCommentSamples(supabase, workshopRow),\n    ]);\n    const firstError =\n        timelineResult.error ??\n        reactionTimelineResult.error ??\n        reactionCountsResult.error ??\n        (commentSampleResult.errorMessage === null ? null : { message: commentSampleResult.errorMessage });\n    if (firstError) {\n        return { analytics: null, errorMessage: firstError.message };\n    }\n\n    const reactionCountsByBucket = groupWorkshopAdminReactionTimelineRows(\n        (reactionTimelineResult.data ?? return { participants, errorMessage: null };\n}\n\n/**\n * Loads all comments for a CSV export, without inheriting the short moderation list used by the interactive screen.\n */\nexport async function []) as WorkshopContentRow[]).map((contentBlock) =>\n            mapWorkshopContentRow(contentBlock, linkClickCountByContentBlockId.get(contentBlock.id) ?? 0),\n        ),\n        errorMessage: null,\n    };\n}\n\n/**\n * Lists the feedback from one workshop only for the administration.\n *\n * Feedback and participants stay separate source records, just as comments and reactions do. The small identity read\n * keeps this list attributable without ever exposing an e-mail address through the participant-facing state route.\n */\nexport async function loadWorkshopAdminFeedback(\n await loadAllSupabaseRows<WorkshopFeedbackRow>(\n        (fromIndex, toIndex) =>\n            supabase\n                .from(WORKSHOP_FEEDBACK_TABLE_NAME)\n .filter((feedback): feedback is WorkshopAdminFeedback => feedback !== null),\n        errorMessage: null,\n    };\n}\n\n/**\n * Loads the message pinned on top of a chat, whatever its age and Note: A pin which could not be loaded must never take the whole room down with it, so a failure is reported as\n *       nothing being pinned.\n */\nasync function return null;\n    }\n\n    const { data, error } = await supabase\n        .from(WORKSHOP_COMMENT_TABLE_NAME)\n        .select(WORKSHOP_COMMENT_COLUMNS)\n        .eq('id', workshopRow.pinned_comment_id)\n        .eq('workshop_id', workshopRow.id)\n        .maybeSingle();\n\n    if (error) {\n        console.error('Failed to load the pinned comment of a workshop:', message on top of a chat or releases the top of that chat again\n *\n * Note: The workshop remembers a single pin, so pinning a message releases the previously pinned one in the same write.\n * Note: Releasing the top only clears this very message, so it never drops a pin which another tab set meanwhile.\n */\nexport async function updatePinnedWorkshopComment(\n    supabase: SupabaseClient,\n 'Pinned comment could not be changed' };\n    }\n\n    return { errorMessage: null };\n}\n\n/**\n * Chooses the one comment the host is answering over the stage, or leaves the stage without a question.\n *\n * Note: The database checks that a selected comment belongs to this room. The stage keeps no copied text: the selected\n *       comment remains the one source of the question in both chat and live presentation.\n */\nexport async function updateWorkshopStageComment(\n    supabase: SupabaseClient,\n    workshopId: string,\n    stageCommentId: string | null,\n): Promise<{ readonly errorMessage: string | null }> {\n    const { error } = await supabase\n        .from(WORKSHOP_TABLE_NAME)\n        .update({ stage_comment_id: stageCommentId })\n        .eq('id', workshopId);\n    if (error) {\n        console.error('Failed to change the comment on a workshop stage:', error.message);\n        return { errorMessage: 'Stage comment could not be changed' };\n    }\n\n    return { errorMessage: null };\n}\n\nexport async function loadWorkshopPublicState(\n    supabase: SupabaseClient,\n    workshopRow: WorkshopRow,\n    participant: WorkshopParticipant,\n    commentSort: WorkshopCommentSort,\n): Promise<LoadedWorkshopPublicState> {\n    const contentVisibilityCutoff = new Date().toISOString();\n    const workshop = mapWorkshopRow(workshopRow);\n    const isWorkshopPast = workshopRow.room_kind === 'workshop' && getWorkshopPhase(workshop) === 'past';\n\n    // Note: The reactions which flew over the stage recently are replayed for somebody entering the room. A room\n    //       without that panel therefore does not load them, exactly as it does not count them.\n    const isReactionsPanelOffered = isWorkshopPanelOffered(\n        workshopRow.room_kind,\n        workshopRow.disabled_panels,\n        'reactions',\n    );\n    const roomCapabilities = getWorkshopKindCapabilities(workshopRow.room_kind);\n    const isStageOffered = roomCapabilities.isStageOffered;\n\n    // Note: The membership decides which materials a member sees, so the room asks about it before it assembles what\n    //       is visible. Every state reload and every heartbeat of every\n *       participant would otherwise count the whole audience for nobody to read.\n * Note: An unavailable count must never take the whole room down with it, so a failure is reported as nobody watching.\n */\nexport async function countWatchingWorkshopParticipants(\n    supabase: SupabaseClient,\n    workshopRow: WorkshopRow,\n): Promise<number> {\n    if (!isWorkshopPanelOffered(workshopRow.room_kind, workshopRow.disabled_panels, 'watching-count')) {\n        return 0;\n    }\n\n    const watchingSince = new Date(Date.now() - WORKSHOP_WATCHING_WINDOW_SECONDS * 1_000).toISOString();\n    const { count, error } = await supabase\n        .from(WORKSHOP_PARTICIPANT_TABLE_NAME)\n        .select('id', { count: 'exact', head: true })\n        .eq('workshop_id', workshopRow.id)\n        .gte('last_seen_at', watchingSince);\n\n    if (error) {\n        console.error('Failed to count the participants watching a workshop:', error.message);\n        return 0;\n    }\n\n    return (count ?? 0) + Math.max(0, workshopRow.artificial_watching_participant_count ?? 0);\n}\n\ntype LoadedWorkshopReactionCounts = {\n    readonly reactionCounts: readonly WorkshopReactionCount[];\n    readonly errorMessage: string | null;\n};\n\n/**\n * Loads the totals shown beside the reactions which a room currently offers\n *\n * Note: When the reactions panel is hidden, nobody can read these totals. Which rooms invite is answered by","originalFile":"## Context\n\nThis repository contains Promptbook landing pages for different businesses,\nuse cases, and audiences. Keep these rules current when behavior changes.\n\n### Public routes\n\n- `/` redirects to `/cs` or `/en` using `Accept-Language`.\n- `/cs` is the Czech homepage and source of truth for homepage structure and copy.\n- `/en` is its English localization.\n- `/pro-mesta`, `/pro-firmy`, `/for-agro`, `/for-industry`, `/ai-supervize`,\n  `/hackathon-factory`, and `/pavol` are specialized landing pages. `/pavol`\n  redirects to `/cs/pavol` or `/en/pavol`; the localized pages are Pavol Hejny's\n  personal pages.\n- `/ai-supervize-mini` is the Czech one-day AI Supervize page. Published terms,\n  prices, capacities, places, FAQs, registration, and participant information\n  come from `/admin/workshops`; with no published term it shows a notice.\n  `/skoleni` redirects there.\n- `/cs/online-workshop` lists free 60-minute online workshops about writing\n  production code with AI agents. Each term has its own subject and description,\n  but all use one registration form. `/cs/online-workshop/dekujeme` is the\n  full-load conversion page; `/participant` is the live room. Its waiting room\n  offers every published term as the same term cards the landing page registers\n  with: running and upcoming ones first, finished ones behind a disclosure.\n  Picking one changes the room being connected to and the `workshop` parameter,\n  without losing the name and e-mail already typed.\n- `/ai-ta-krajta` reads episodes hourly from podcast RSS and YouTube feeds and\n  merges their host rosters with `businesses/ai-ta-krajta/aiTaKrajtaEpisodes.json`. Its shared platform list exposes\n  the publisher's direct RSS feed for custom podcast applications, and page metadata advertises it as\n  `application/rss+xml`.\n  Each episode lists every credited person by name, and every person any source\n  credits has a card in `aiTaKrajtaPeople.ts`, which a test keeps in step, so a\n  credited person never misses their portrait and the filter cannot lose them.\n  It keeps exact episode counts but labels subscriptions and listening hours as\n  estimates. The fixed mini-player, newest-episode header button, person/search/\n  episode/play/archive/collaboration filters, and section hash are shareable as\n  query/hash state; the snake game is local state. Person clicks filter episodes.\n  Everyone in the roster shows a normalized, transparent PNG portrait. The source\n  crop is recorded by `scripts/_cutAiTaKrajtaPeoplePortraits.mjs`, from the\n  episode cover the show itself published them on or from the picture they publish\n  of themselves when no cover carries them; the final alpha PNG is named by the\n  roster and a test verifies its format and transparent pixels. Portrait frames\n  supply subtle, stable neutral-gradient variations and a restrained hover cue,\n  so photographed backgrounds never compete with the page. The one people list\n  is drawn anew\n  for every visit, weighted by how many episodes of the archive name each\n  person, so somebody heard often comes up high far more often than someone in\n  one díl without the list ever becoming a ranking. The draw is local state and\n  is made in the browser; the page itself is built in the order the draw leans\n  towards, from the most often named person to the least often named one, so the\n  browser hydrates into the list it was sent.\n  Collaboration submissions use `/admin/contacts`. Its tab icon is the page's\n  own snake drawing in `/ai-ta-krajta/logo.svg` and `.png`; SVG corners are\n  rounded and transparent, while the raster fills its square. That drawing is\n  traced off the cover artwork of the show and recorded once in\n  `businesses/ai-ta-krajta/aiTaKrajtaMarkArtwork.ts`, together with the\n  measurements of the animal along its own length. The snake of the minigame\n  starts in exactly that shape, in the frame the still logo occupied, and only\n  then eases into the proportions, colours and speed of a game snake.\n  A seven-cell Promptbook coder terminal floats in the bottom-right corner and\n  clears the player and cookie controls. It types `$ ptbk`, then animates an\n  ASCII octopus in response to pointer, focus, scrolling, and the snake terrarium.\n  It stays still for reduced motion and pauses its clock in hidden tabs. The\n  badge and the shared footer credit link to `https://coder.ptbk.io/`.\n- `/ai-ta-krajta/media-kit` and `/ai-ta-krajta/branding` are the two pages beside\n  the podcast. They are named once, in `AI_TA_KRAJTA_SUBPAGES`, which the footer\n  lists and which they point at each other through, so no link can name a page\n  differently than the page names itself. Both wear the same compact header,\n  section heading and footer as each other. The brand kit hands out the logo the\n  site already serves at `/ai-ta-krajta/logo.svg`, `.png` and the cover artwork,\n  publishes no colour outside `AI_TA_KRAJTA_COLORS`, and says how the name is\n  written; it asks for nothing and sends visitors to the media-kit form.\n- `/cs/komunita` is the permanent Czech community room. It has chat, polls,\n  projects, materials, and published terms, but no schedule, stage, or live\n  updates. Terms show event kind, format/place, price, and status. A term with a\n  live room links there; otherwise it links to its landing page. The calendar\n  opens on the member's month, can filter by day, and uses the same terms and\n  statuses as the cards. Empty days cannot be selected; an empty month is only\n  selected when the member's month has no terms. The room offers Google Calendar\n  and `webcal:` subscriptions.\n- `/cs/komunita/projects` is the full project gallery, ordered by upvotes.\n  `/cs/komunita/projects/<project_id>` shows scraped project details and a\n  moderated discussion. Project-room sessions derive from the community session;\n  the author moderates their own discussion.\n- `/cs/komunita/clenstvi` offers free community access and the 199 Kč monthly\n  membership. Webinars remain free; paid access adds recordings, archive,\n  materials, extra content, priority questions, and Discord/community features.\n  The page is prefilled from `fullname` and `email`, supports community discount\n  codes, has no new annual plan or trial, and allows cancellation.\n- `/cs/komunita/calendar.ics` publishes the same terms by stable slug, so moved\n  or renamed terms update existing subscriptions. It contains only event terms\n  and public destinations, never subscriber identity.\n- `/admin/workshops` manages terms of every event kind, participants, comments,\n  reactions, content, attached community polls, and settings. Every term says both\n  of its audiences: the people registered on the landing page of its event, and\n  the people who entered its room. A room which is no term of an event says\n  nothing about registrations at all. The registration block opens the exact\n  filtered `/admin/contacts` list and its shared CSV, vCard, and Book exports;\n  it never creates a second contact table or serializer in workshop administration.\n- `/admin/community` manages the permanent community, including polls, project\n  moderation, participants, memberships, payments, and room analytics.\n- `/admin/shortener` manages public short links, QR/UTM output, destinations,\n  notes, search/filter/sort state, and private click history. Links are served\n  by `/[shortcode]`; `/shortener` redirects to the admin page.\n- `/admin/login` authenticates the single `admin` account with `ADMIN_PASSWORD`\n  and a signed session cookie. All `/admin/*` pages and APIs require\n  `requireAdminSignedIn`. `/admin` is the post-login dashboard.\n- Other public/legal routes include `/contact`, `/data-deletion`, `/privacy`,\n  `/terms`, `/dekujeme`, `/branding`, and the routes under `/k`, `/old`, and\n  `/test`.\n\n### Shared community and workshop behavior\n\n- Rooms lead to each other in both directions, through one identity hand-off. The\n  community lists the terms and opens the room of each; an invited workshop room\n  places its community link beside its materials as a special material for every\n  participant, regardless of paid membership. Both carry the connected member's\n  name and email on, and an incomplete identity carries nothing rather than half\n  of it. Which rooms invite is answered by\n  `lib/workshops/workshopKindCapabilities.ts`; the community and project\n  discussions do not. The invitation names the community's sections by the names\n  the community itself uses.\n- Community polls attached to workshops are shared. A normalized email gives a\n  member one vote across the community and all attached workshops. Workshops\n  may display and accept votes, but the community owns administration.\n- The participant room owns the membership badge and popup. Community and live\n  workshop rooms use the same membership for the connecting email, and checkout\n  returns to the room where it started. Membership is offered only by room kinds\n  listed in `lib/workshops/workshopKindCapabilities.ts`; project discussions do\n  not offer it.\n- Members can open Stripe Customer Portal from the popup. In-app cancellation\n  stops only the next renewal, preserves access through the paid period, appears\n  in the badge, and can be reversed before that period ends.\n- A full-price-for-the-whole-term discount is a voucher: atomically consume it,\n  create membership immediately, ask for no card, and create no Stripe renewal.\n  A limited-month discount still opens checkout because the regular price returns.\n  Stripe webhooks update completed, cancelled, failed, and late payments. With no\n  Stripe key, hide membership; with test keys, identify the test payment gate.\n- Community projects use a URL-first metadata wizard. Ordinary submissions await\n  moderation; trusted members and moderators are approved immediately. Pending\n  projects remain visible to their author and moderators.\n- A live workshop room has countdown, YouTube stage, reactions, watching count,\n  moderated chat, timed materials, and attached poll aggregates. An open-ended\n  term runs until its recorded end; its stage does not end automatically. Admins\n  can select, replace, clear, or create the displayed comment through the same\n  private realtime channel used by reactions.\n- A term can be about a project. The connection is one value — GitHub repository,\n  the default branch, and one or more branch patterns such as `main`, `client-*`,\n  `feature/*`, or `*` for all branches, plus an optional deployment URL — so it is\n  set, changed, and unset at once and neither branch selection nor deployment\n  outlives its repository. Room kinds which offer it are named in\n  `lib/workshops/workshopKindCapabilities.ts`. The room shows the repository as a\n  special material beside its ordinary materials for every participant, with its\n  links and newest commits, marking those which arrive while a participant watches;\n  a newly found commit is broadcast to active rooms and appears on the stage for\n  ten seconds. A selection resolving to multiple branches is shown as a commit\n  graph. Commits come from the public commit feed or keyless API, pooled once per\n  server and cached through the revalidation window; an unreadable feed still\n  leaves the room naming its project.\n- A workshop can carry one public presentation URL for a PDF, PowerPoint file, or\n  GitHub Markdown page. The room renders it beside ordinary materials through the\n  shared material card, primary action, and QR code, for every participant without\n  making it timed or membership-gated content.\n- Paid-only materials are decided on the server in one pass. Members receive\n  unlocked material; others receive only the published titles as an offer. An\n  untitled item is not named, items are not named before their unlock time, and a\n  room without membership hides paid-only items without naming them.\n- After a workshop ends, its recording is server-gated to members. Others receive\n  the published teaser, or a generic offer when no teaser exists; a term without\n  a recording offers nothing.\n- Trusted participants remain invisible and their messages are auto-approved.\n  Moderators see pending messages, can approve/reject/correct/pin them, and can\n  trust or silence authors. Workshop and community moderators are appointed in\n  `/admin/workshops`; project authors moderate their own discussions.\n- The room records whether each open browser is actively or passively attended\n  from pointer, typing, scroll, and touch activity. Admin analytics distinguish\n  active computer users from merely open tabs with dashed audience lines.\n- The community's compact gallery shows its five highest-upvoted approved projects\n  and links to the full gallery. Community landing content is read from the live\n  room: expose only anonymous totals, approved messages, and shared projects;\n  show member first names only. If the room cannot be read, show less content,\n  not an error. Landing-page reactions are estimates based on recent room data.\n\n### Administration and data rules\n\n- Event kinds are defined once in `lib/events/eventTypes.ts`; adding one should\n  not require database migration or page-specific duplication. Terms ask for kind,\n  online/place format, price, and capacity. Each kind also names where its landing\n  page records registrations, which is the `placeName` of the contacts it gathers.\n- Which term a registration belongs to is decided once, in\n  `lib/workshops/workshopRegistrations.ts`. A term is recognised by its slug, by\n  its Prague day, and by the moment it begins at, so registrations written before\n  terms had slugs keep counting. Registration forms write the term through the\n  same line prefixes that rule reads back. Contacts are still gathered, recorded\n  and shown only by `/admin/contacts`; counting reads nothing but their notes.\n  The registration actions in workshop administration carry that same term filter\n  into the contacts list and its exports.\n- Workshop polls are read-only in workshop administration. Creating a new event\n  publishes it by default; duplicating an event keeps it published unless the\n  source is unpublished. Duplicating a workshop preserves its connections to\n  the already existing attached polls; it creates no polls, options, votes, or room history. Stage settings contain\n  the live stream and recording teaser, presentation settings the public presentation\n  address, and project settings the repository the term is about, written as an\n  address or as `owner/name`, together with its branch patterns. Deleting a workshop is a soft deletion: its room\n  data and attached\n  community polls stay stored, but the term leaves normal public and administrative\n  lists and no longer holds its slug for a replacement. An end may be empty;\n  admins can record, adjust, clear, and reopen it. Overview analytics are zoomable and share their\n  room, section, lines, reaction, zoom, and keyword metrics through query params.\n- Community administration is the workshop dashboard restricted to the\n  `community` room kind: no room picker, schedule, stage, reactions, or address.\n  Its membership view filters Stripe lifecycle, prices, discounts, identifiers,\n  dates, test/live mode, and links to the exact Stripe checkout/subscription.\n  Community analytics cover all measured time and member details show seen times.\n- Shortener search, provenance filters, sorting, and selected click history live\n  in GET parameters. Editing changes only shortcode, destinations, note, and\n  landing page; deletion also deletes recorded clicks.\n\n### Database and verification\n\n- Put database changes in `migrations/*.sql`. Startup and\n  `npm run migrate-database` run `_initialize.sql`, then migrations in filename\n  order, recording immutable filenames and checksums in `public.\"Migration\"`.\n  Changed or missing migrations fail, as do queries requiring an unapplied one.\n- `npm run test-types` must build before `tsc` to refresh `.next/types`.\n- `npm run test-e2e` uses the Next.js development server; first-request compile\n  headroom belongs in `playwright.config.ts`, not individual tests. E2E tests are\n  independent and each archives one recording in `tests/e2e/videos/`, retaining\n  only recent runs.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":114,"oldLines":7,"newStart":114,"newLines":12,"lines":[" - Rooms lead to each other in both directions, through one identity hand-off.
